proposals.before: Nineteen people tell Mao Sui: Mister ascend.
proposals.after: The nineteen men said to Mao Sui: “Master, go up.”
proposals.reason: The literal field is an ungrammatical word-for-word fragment; this restores the subject, addressee, and imperative.

proposals.before: Today out speak vertical, day middle not decide, why?"
proposals.after: We began speaking of the alliance at sunrise, yet by noon no decision had been reached. Why?
proposals.reason: The literal field is an ungrammatical calque; this restores the temporal contrast and the alliance sense of 從.

proposals.before: Mao Sui press sword before: Wang so scold Sui, with Chu country crowd.
proposals.after: Mao Sui advanced with his hand on his sword and said: “Your Majesty rebukes me because you rely on Chu's great multitude.”
proposals.reason: The literal field leaves Chinese words untranslated and obscures Mao Sui's action and the king's reliance on Chu.

proposals.before: The next year Qin attacked the king again, and the king had no rescue."
proposals.after: Next year Qin will attack Your Majesty again, and you will have no one to rescue you.”
proposals.reason: The literal field incorrectly shifts the prediction into past tense; 來年 and 復攻 require a future warning.

proposals.before: This did not minister dare take responsibility."
proposals.after: This is not a responsibility your minister dares to assume.”
proposals.reason: The literal field is syntactically broken; this gives the negative and ministerial self-reference their normal sense.

proposals.before: Qin Zhao construct difficulty yet world all pleased, why?
proposals.after: When Qin and Zhao become embroiled in conflict, the whole world is pleased. Why?
proposals.reason: The literal field mechanically renders 構難 as “construct difficulty”; the phrase means to become embroiled in conflict.

proposals.before: Zhao and perish, what Qin scheme!
proposals.after: Zhao is about to perish—what use will Qin's plans be then?
proposals.reason: The literal field is an ungrammatical calque; this restores the imminent-peril statement and rhetorical question.

decisions.reason: 十九人謂毛遂曰：「先生上。」 needs a finite past narrative with addressee and imperative; the broken calque “Nineteen people tell… Mister ascend” is not English, and “The nineteen men said… Master, go up” restores subject, verb, and 先生上 without inventing content.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十九人謂毛遂曰：「先生上。」

decisions.reason: 今日出而言從，日中不決，何也 records sunrise-to-noon talks about the vertical alliance (從) with no decision; the word-for-word “Today out speak vertical…” is unreadable, and the proposed English restores that temporal contrast and sense of 從.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今日出而言從，日中不決，何也？

decisions.after: Mao Sui advanced, gripping his sword, and said: “Your Majesty rebukes me because of Chu's great multitude.
decisions.reason: 按劍而前曰 and 王之所以叱遂者，以楚國之眾也 do need repair of the broken calque, but the proposal adds “rely on” (恃 belongs to the next unit) and wrongly closes the still-open quotation; keep advance-with-sword and “because of Chu's great multitude” without inventing reliance or ending the speech.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 毛遂按劍而前曰：「王之所以叱遂者，以楚國之眾也。

decisions.reason: 來年秦復攻王，王無救矣 is Yu Qing’s forward warning (“next year Qin will attack again”), not a past event; the original past-tense literal falsifies 來年/復攻, and the proposed future warning matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 來年秦復攻王，王無救矣。

decisions.reason: 此非臣之所敢任也 is Zhao Hao’s closing disclaimer that the projected outcome is not a responsibility he dares assume; the broken “This did not minister dare…” is not English, and “your minister” correctly renders court 臣.
秦趙構難而天下皆說，何也 uses 構難 for becoming embroiled in conflict and 說 for being pleased; “construct difficulty” is a false calque, and the proposed rendering matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 夫秦趙構難而天下皆說，何也？

decisions.reason: 趙且亡，何秦之圖乎 pairs imminent peril (且亡) with a rhetorical question about Qin’s designs; the calque “Zhao and perish, what Qin scheme!” is broken, and the proposed English restores both parts without changing the counsel.
